name: Connaught Bridge Power Station
status_detail: Operational · redeveloped combined-cycle plant commissioned February 2016
summary: One of Malaysia's oldest power stations, opened in 1953 near Kampong Jawa in Klang and redeveloped by TNB into a 375 MW combined-cycle plant completed in 2016.

scale.label: Current capacity
scale.value: 375 MW combined cycle (1 gas turbine + 1 steam turbine)

scale.label: Pre-redevelopment capacity
scale.value: 895 MW (315 MW combined cycle + 4 x 130 MW open cycle)

why_it_matters: A 1953-era station that shows how the Klang Valley's legacy thermal fleet is being recycled site-by-site instead of expanded on greenfield land. Its gas-fired output sits close to the Klang industrial belt and the grid corridor feeding Selangor's data centre load.
questions_to_follow: Will TNB pursue a further combined-cycle replacement at Connaught Bridge as units age out?
How much longer do the remaining pre-2016 assets stay on the system?
location_precision: Station site at Kampong Jawa, Klang. Coordinates from Global Energy Monitor (listed as exact).

history.event: Opened by High Commissioner Sir Gerald Templer; one of the country's oldest power stations.
Redeveloped combined-cycle plant commissioned, cutting installed capacity from 895 MW to 375 MW.
